chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Ibrahim ibn Maymun has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, the cloth seller from Herat and a freed servant of the family of Al-Zubayr.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونَ: Ibrahim ibn Maymun, a prominent Shia narrator
key_terms.بَيَّاعِ الْهَرَوِيِّ: The cloth seller from Herat, a descriptive title for the narrator
key_terms.مَوْلَى آلِ الزُّبَيْرِ: Freed servant of the family of Al-Zubayr, indicating social status
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Ibrahim ibn Maymun's hadiths in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* provides a specific *isnad* (chain of transmission) for narrations by Ibrahim ibn Maymun that were not included in the main text, thereby ensuring their authenticity and linking them to the author, Shaykh al-Saduq. It highlights the scholarly practice of preserving alternative transmission lines to maintain the integrity of hadith literature, specifically connecting the narrator to the broader network of early Shia scholars.
